`Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[package]
name = "dmaguard"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.82"
authors = ["grimh3xx"]
description = "dmaguard — read-only DMA attack-surface auditor: IOMMU / VT-d / AMD-Vi state, ACPI DMAR & IVRS parsing, Kernel DMA Protection, Thunderbolt security levels"
repository = "https://github.com/grimh3xx/dmaguard"
license = "MIT"
keywords = ["security", "iommu", "dma", "thunderbolt", "blue-team"]
categories = ["command-line-utilities"]
readme = "README.md"

[dependencies]
clap = { version = "4.5", features = ["derive"] }
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
owo-colors = { version = "4", features = ["supports-colors"] }
anstream = "0.6"

[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]
windows-sys = { version = "0.59", features = [
    "Wdk_System_SystemInformation",
    "Win32_Foundation",
    "Win32_System_Registry",
    "Win32_System_SystemInformation",
] }

[profile.release]
opt-level = 3
lto = true
strip = true
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"

```

`README.md`:

```md
<img src="docs/banner.svg" alt="dmaguard" width="100%">

[![build](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/grimh3xx/dmaguard/build.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&labelColor=111826&label=build)](https://github.com/grimh3xx/dmaguard/actions)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/github/license/grimh3xx/dmaguard?style=flat-square&labelColor=111826&color=22D3EE)](LICENSE)
![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-2021-3B82F6?style=flat-square&labelColor=111826)
![platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows%20%7C%20Linux-x64-22D3EE?style=flat-square&labelColor=111826)
![read-only](https://img.shields.io/badge/read--only-no%20changes-34D399?style=flat-square&labelColor=111826)

**Can a device you plug in read your memory?** dmaguard answers that
question. It parses the firmware's ACPI **DMAR** (Intel VT-d) and **IVRS**
(AMD-Vi) tables directly, then checks how the OS actually uses the IOMMU:
**Kernel DMA Protection** on Windows; IOMMU domains, boot parameters,
**Thunderbolt security levels** and external PCIe devices on Linux.


<p align="center"><img src="docs/demo.svg" alt="dmaguard demo" width="100%"></p>

<sub>Recorded from real output against `tests/fixtures/laptop` (Thunderbolt security `none`, `iommu=pt`, DMAR without the DMA opt-in) built by `tools/make_fixture.py`. Regenerate with `python3 tools/gen_demo.py`.</sub>

## Findings

| ID | Severity | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| DMA-001 | high | No IOMMU active / available |
| DMA-002 | medium | IOMMU in passthrough (identity domains, `iommu=pt`) |
| DMA-003 | medium | Firmware does not opt in to pre-boot DMA protection (DMAR `DMA_CTRL_PLATFORM_OPT_IN` / IVRS IVinfo bit 1). This is the root cause behind "Kernel DMA Protection: Off" |
| DMA-004 | high/medium | Kernel DMA Protection off (Windows) / Thunderbolt `iommu_dma_protection=0` (Linux) |
| DMA-005 | high | Thunderbolt security level `none` without an IOMMU backstop |
| DMA-006 | high | IOMMU disabled on the kernel command line |
| DMA-007 | medium | No interrupt remapping (MSI injection bypass) |
| DMA-008 | medium/info | Windows DMA device-enumeration policy |
| DMA-009 | low | FireWire controller active |
| DMA-010 | info | RMRR identity-mapped regions on devices other than legacy GPU/USB |
| DMA-011 | low | Invalid ACPI table checksum |
| DMA-012 | high | No DMAR/IVRS table at all (VT-d / AMD-Vi off in firmware) |
| DMA-013 | info | External (removable) PCIe devices attached |
| DMA-016 | low | Lazy IOTLB invalidation (`DMA-FQ`) |

### A note on Windows

`SystemVsmProtectionInformation` reports whether the **hypervisor** has an
IOMMU. That can read *available / in use* while external devices are
unprotected. Kernel DMA Protection, as msinfo32 shows it, is
`SystemDmaGuardPolicyInformation`. dmaguard reads both and explains the gap.
On real hardware, a set IOMMU flag together with Kernel DMA Protection Off
traced back to the firmware's IVRS opt-in bit being clear.

## Install

**Pre-built binaries** (from [Releases](https://github.com/grimh3xx/dmaguard/releases/latest)):

```sh
# Linux x64
curl -fsSL -o dmaguard https://github.com/grimh3xx/dmaguard/releases/latest/download/dmaguard-linux-x64
chmod +x dmaguard && sudo mv dmaguard /usr/local/bin/
```

```powershell
# Windows x64 (PowerShell)
iwr https://github.com/grimh3xx/dmaguard/releases/latest/download/dmaguard-windows-x64.exe -OutFile dmaguard.exe
.\dmaguard.exe --help
```

**From source** (Rust 1.82+):

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/grimh3xx/dmaguard
```

Linux needs root to read the ACPI DMAR/IVRS tables. The binaries are not code-signed, so SmartScreen or Defender may flag
them heuristically. Build from source if you prefer to verify.

## Usage

```sh
dmaguard                         # audit this machine (Linux: root for ACPI tables)
dmaguard --dmar DMAR.bin         # parse a dumped table (acpidump -b, GetSystemFirmwareTable)
dmaguard --ivrs IVRS.bin
dmaguard --root /mnt/snapshot    # Linux: offline /proc + /sys tree
dmaguard --json | --sarif
```

ACPI tables are read from `/sys/firmware/acpi/tables` on Linux and through
`GetSystemFirmwareTable('ACPI', ...)` on Windows, then parsed in-tree. Exit
codes follow the worst finding (0–4).

## Build

```sh
cargo build --release
cargo build --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu
```

`SECURITY.md`:

```md
# Security policy

dmaguard is a read-only auditing tool. If you find a bug that makes it write, modify,
or execute anything on the audited system, or a parser crash on crafted input,
please report it privately through **GitHub → Security → Report a vulnerability**
on this repository rather than opening a public issue.

Supported version: the latest release.

```

mode (14 identity-mapped group(s))</text></g><g id="l42"><text x="0.0" fill="#C5CFDD" textLength="772.2" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">             Identity domains give devices 1:1 access to physical memory — the IOMMU is present but</text></g><g id="l43"><text x="0.0" fill="#C5CFDD" textLength="756.6" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">             not isolating them. Thunderbolt/untrusted devices are still forced into DMA domains,</text></g><g id="l44"><text x="0.0" fill="#C5CFDD" textLength="273.0" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">             internal ones are not.</text></g><g id="l45"><text x="101.4" fill="#7C8AA0" textLength="23.4" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">src</text><text x="132.6" fill="#7C8AA0" textLength="241.8" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">/sys/kernel/iommu_groups/*/type</text></g><g id="l46"><text x="101.4" fill="#34D399" textLength="23.4" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">fix</text><text x="124.8" fill="#C5CFDD" textLength="592.8" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs"> Drop iommu=pt / iommu.passthrough=1 unless required for performance; prefer</text></g><g id="l47"><text x="0.0" fill="#C5CFDD" textLength="249.6" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">                 iommu.strict=1.</text></g><g id="l48"><text x="31.2" fill="#FBBF24" font-weight="700" textLength="62.4" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">MEDIUM  </text><text x="101.4" fill="#60A5FA" textLength="54.6" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">DMA-003</text><text x="171.6" fill="#C5CFDD" font-weight="700" textLength="452.4" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">Firmware does not opt in to pre-boot DMA protection (DMAR)</text></g><g id="l49"><text x="0.0" fill="#C5CFDD" textLength="756.6" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">             DMA_CTRL_PLATFORM_OPT_IN is clear: firmware does not promise to keep VT-d protecting</text></g><g id="l50"><text x="0.0" fill="#C5CFDD" textLength="702.0" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">             memory across the boot-to-OS handoff. Windows Kernel DMA Protection and Linux</text></g><g id="l51"><text x="0.0" fill="#C5CFDD" textLength="741.0" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">             Thunderbolt `iommu_dma_protection` stay off on such platforms, and devices can DMA</text></g><g id="l52"><text x="0.0" fill="#C5CFDD" textLength="241.8" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">             during early boot.</text></g><g id="l53"><text x="101.4" fill="#7C8AA0" textLength="23.4" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">src</text><text x="132.6" fill="#7C8AA0" textLength="70.2" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">acpi/DMAR</text></g><g id="l54"><text x="101.4" fill="#34D399" textLength="23.4" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">fix</text><text x="124.8" fill="#C5CFDD" textLength="608.4" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs"> Update firmware; enable 'Pre-boot DMA protection' / 'Kernel DMA Protection' /</text></g><g id="l55"><text x="0.0" fill="#C5CFDD" textLength="514.8" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">                 'Thunderbolt DMA protection' in setup if offered.</text></g><g id="l56"><text x="31.2" fill="#22D3EE" textLength="62.4" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">LOW     </text><text x="101.4" fill="#60A5FA" textLength="54.6" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">DMA-016</text><text x="171.6" fill="#C5CFDD" font-weight="700" textLength="358.8" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">Lazy IOTLB invalidation on 3 group(s) (DMA-FQ)</text></g><g id="l57"><text x="0.0" fill="#C5CFDD" textLength="772.2" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">             Flush queues defer IOTLB invalidation, leaving a short window where a device can still</text></g><g id="l58"><text x="0.0" fill="#C5CFDD" textLength="257.4" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">             reach freed buffers.</text></g><g id="l59"><text x="101.4" fill="#34D399" textLength="23.4" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">fix</text><text x="124.8" fill="#C5CFDD" textLength="553.8" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs"> Boot with iommu.strict=1 on machines exposed to untrusted peripherals.</text></g><g id="l60"><text x="31.2" fill="#7C8AA0" textLength="62.4" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">INFO    </text><text x="101.4" fill="#60A5FA" textLength="54.6" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">DMA-010</text><text x="171.6" fill="#C5CFDD" font-weight="700" textLength="421.2" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">1 RMRR identity-mapped region(s) on non-legacy devices</text></g><g id="l61"><text x="0.0" fill="#C5CFDD" textLength="764.4" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">             Reserved Memory Region Reporting forces identity mappings that the IOMMU cannot fully</text></g><g id="l62"><text x="0.0" fill="#C5CFDD" textLength="608.4" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">             isolate. Expected for integrated graphics/USB; unusual elsewhere.</text></g><g id="l63"><text x="101.4" fill="#7C8AA0" textLength="7.8" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">·</text><text x="117.0" fill="#7C8AA0" textLength="358.8" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">1 external (removable) PCIe device(s) attached</text></g><g id="l65"><text x="0.0" fill="#C5CFDD" textLength="624.0" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs"> `src/acpi.rs`:

```rs
//! ACPI DMAR (Intel VT-d) and IVRS (AMD-Vi) table parsing. Both tables are
//! read raw — from sysfs, GetSystemFirmwareTable, or a dump file — so the
//! same code runs everywhere and can be unit-tested with synthetic tables.

use serde::Serialize;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct Header {
    pub signature: String,
    pub length: u32,
    pub revision: u8,
    pub checksum_ok: bool,
    pub oem_id: String,
    pub oem_table_id: String,
}

fn u16_at(b: &[u8], o: usize) -> Option<u16> {
    Some(u16::from_le_bytes(b.get(o..o + 2)?.try_into().ok()?))
}

fn u32_at(b: &[u8], o: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    Some(u32::from_le_bytes(b.get(o..o + 4)?.try_into().ok()?))
}

fn u64_at(b: &[u8], o: usize) -> Option<u64> {
    Some(u64::from_le_bytes(b.get(o..o + 8)?.try_into().ok()?))
}

fn text(b: &[u8]) -> String {
    String::from_utf8_lossy(b)
        .trim_end_matches(['\0', ' '])
        .to_string()
}

pub fn header(t: &[u8]) -> Option<Header> {
    if t.len() < 36 {
        return None;
    }
    let length = u32_at(t, 4)?;
    let body = t.get(..length as usize)?;
    Some(Header {
        signature: text(&t[0..4]),
        length,
        revision: t[8],
        checksum_ok: body.iter().fold(0u8, |a, b| a.wrapping_add(*b)) == 0,
        oem_id: text(&t[10..16]),
        oem_table_id: text(&t[16..24]),
    })
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct Rmrr {
    pub segment: u16,
    pub base: String,
    pub limit: String,
    pub devices: Vec<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct Dmar {
    pub header: Header,
    pub host_address_width: u8,
    pub intr_remap: bool,
    pub x2apic_opt_out: bool,
    /// DMA_CTRL_PLATFORM_OPT_IN_FLAG: firmware kept DMA protection on through
    /// the boot-to-OS handoff. Windows Kernel DMA Protection and Linux
    /// Thunderbolt `iommu_dma_protection` both require it.
    pub dma_ctrl_platform_opt_in: bool,
    pub drhd_units: usize,
    pub include_pci_all: bool,
    pub rmrrs: Vec<Rmrr>,
    pub atsr: usize,
    pub satc: usize,
}

/// Device scope entries: Type u8, Length u8, Reserved u16, EnumerationID u8,
/// StartBus u8, then (Device u8, Function u8) path pairs.
fn scopes(b: &[u8]) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut p = 0;
    while p + 6 <= b.len() {
        let len = b[p + 1] as usize;
        if len < 6 || p + len > b.len() {
            break;
        }
        let kind = match b[p] {
            1 => "pci-endpoint",
            2 => "pci-bridge",
            3 => "ioapic",
            4 => "hpet",
            5 => "acpi-namespace",
            _ => "other",
        };
        let bus = b[p + 5];
        let path: Vec<String> = b[p + 6..p + len]
            .chunks_exact(2)
            .map(|df| format!("{:02x}.{}", df[0], df[1]))
            .collect();
        out.push(format!("{kind} {bus:02x}:{}", path.join("/")));
        p += len;
    }
    out
}

pub fn parse_dmar(t: &[u8]) -> Option<Dmar> {
    let header = header(t)?;
    if header.signature != "DMAR" || t.len() < 48 {
        return None;
    }
    let flags = t[37];
    let mut d = Dmar {
        host_address_width: t[36].wrapping_add(1),
        intr_remap: flags & 0x1 != 0,
        x2apic_opt_out: flags & 0x2 != 0,
        dma_ctrl_platform_opt_in: flags & 0x4 != 0,
        drhd_units: 0,
        include_pci_all: false,
        rmrrs: Vec::new(),
        atsr: 0,
        satc: 0,
        header,
    };
    let end = (d.header.length as usize).min(t.len());
    let mut p = 48;
    while p + 4 <= end {
        let typ = u16_at(t, p)?;
        let len = u16_at(t, p + 2)? as usize;
        if len < 4 || p + len > end {
            break;
        }
        let s = &t[p..p + len];
        match typ {
            0 => {
                d.drhd_units += 1;
                d.include_pci_all |= s.get(4).is_some_and(|f| f & 1 != 0);
            }
            1 if len >= 24 => d.rmrrs.push(Rmrr {
                segment: u16_at(s, 6)?,
                base: format!("{:#x}", u64_at(s, 8)?),
                limit: format!("{:#x}", u64_at(s, 16)?),
                devices: scopes(&s[24..]),
            }),
            2 => d.atsr += 1,
            5 => d.satc += 1,
            _ => {}
        }
        p += len;
    }
    Some(d)
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct Ivrs {
    pub header: Header,
    /// IVinfo[1]: platform requests DMA remapping be kept on for pre-boot
    /// protection (AMD analogue of DMA_CTRL_PLATFORM_OPT_IN).
    pub dma_remap_opt_in: bool,
    pub efr_supported: bool,
    pub ivhd_blocks: usize,
    pub ivmd_blocks: usize,
}

pub fn parse_ivrs(t: &[u8]) -> Option<Ivrs> {
    let header = header(t)?;
    if header.signature != "IVRS" || t.len() < 48 {
        return None;
    }
    let ivinfo = u32_at(t, 36)?;
    let mut v = Ivrs {
        dma_remap_opt_in: ivinfo & 0x2 != 0,
        efr_supported: ivinfo & 0x1 != 0,
        ivhd_blocks: 0,
        ivmd_blocks: 0,
        header,
    };
    let end = (v.header.length as usize).min(t.len());
    let mut p = 48;
    while p + 4 <= end {
        let typ = t[p];
        let len = u16_at(t, p + 2)? as usize;
        if len < 4 || p + len > end {
            break;
        }
        match typ {
            0x10 | 0x11 | 0x40 => v.ivhd_blocks += 1,
            0x20..=0x22 => v.ivmd_blocks += 1,
            _ => {}
        }
        p += len;
    }
    Some(v)
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub mod build {
    pub fn table(sig: &[u8; 4], extra_hdr: &[u8], body: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut t = Vec::new();
        t.extend_from_slice(sig);
        t.extend_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes());
        t.push(1); // revision
        t.push(0); // checksum, patched below
        t.extend_from_slice(b"GRIMH3");
        t.extend_from_slice(b"TESTTBL ");
        t.extend_from_slice(&[0u8; 12]);
        t.extend_from_slice(extra_hdr);
        t.extend_from_slice(body);
        let len = t.len() as u32;
        t[4..8].copy_from_slice(&len.to_le_bytes());
        let sum = t.iter().fold(0u8, |a, b| a.wrapping_add(*b));
        t[9] = 0u8.wrapping_sub(sum);
        t
    }

    pub fn dmar(flags: u8, with_rmrr: bool) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut hdr = vec![38, flags];
        hdr.extend_from_slice(&[0u8; 10]);
        let mut body = Vec::new();
        // DRHD, INCLUDE_PCI_ALL
        body.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes());
        body.extend_from_slice(&16u16.to_le_bytes());
        body.extend_from_slice(&[1, 0, 0, 0]);
        body.extend_from_slice(&0xfed9_0000u64.to_le_bytes());
        if with_rmrr {
            body.extend_from_slice(&1u16.to_le_bytes());
            body.extend_from_slice(&32u16.to_le_bytes());
            body.extend_from_slice(&[0, 0, 0, 0]);
            body.extend_from_slice(&0x7c00_0000u64.to_le_bytes());
            body.extend_from_slice(&0x7fff_ffffu64.to_le_bytes());
            body.extend_from_slice(&[1, 8, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x14, 0]); // endpoint 00:14.0 (xHCI)
        }
        table(b"DMAR", &hdr, &body)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::build::*;
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn dmar_flags_and_structures() {
        let d = parse_dmar(&dmar(0b101, true)).unwrap();
        assert!(d.header.checksum_ok);
        assert_eq!(d.header.oem_id, "GRIMH3");
        assert_eq!(d.host_address_width, 39);
        assert!(d.intr_remap && d.dma_ctrl_platform_opt_in && !d.x2apic_opt_out);
        assert_eq!(d.drhd_units, 1);
        assert!(d.include_pci_all);
        assert_eq!(d.rmrrs.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(d.rmrrs[0].devices, vec!["pci-endpoint 00:14.0"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn dmar_bad_checksum_detected() {
        let mut t = dmar(0, false);
        t[40] ^= 0xff;
        assert!(!parse_dmar(&t).unwrap().header.checksum_ok);
    }

    #[test]
    fn ivrs_opt_in_bit() {
        let mut hdr = 0x2u32.to_le_bytes().to_vec();
        hdr.extend_from_slice(&[0u8; 8]);
        let mut body = vec![0x40, 0, 8, 0];
        body.extend_from_slice(&[0u8; 4]);
        let v = parse_ivrs(&table(b"IVRS", &hdr, &body)).unwrap();
        assert!(v.dma_remap_opt_in);
        assert_eq!(v.ivhd_blocks, 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn truncated_is_none() {
        assert!(parse_dmar(&[0u8; 20]).is_none());
        assert!(parse_dmar(&table(b"APIC", &[0; 12], &[])).is_none());
    }
}

```rs
//! DMA attack-surface findings, shared between Linux and Windows.

use serde::Serialize;

use crate::acpi::{Dmar, Ivrs};
use crate::report::{Finding, Severity};

#[derive(Debug, Default, Serialize)]
pub struct Firmware {
    pub dmar: Option<Dmar>,
    pub ivrs: Option<Ivrs>,
    /// Tables could not be read (e.g. not root); absence means nothing then.
    pub unreadable: Option<String>,
}

pub fn firmware(fw: &Firmware, x86: bool) -> Vec<Finding> {
    let mut f = Vec::new();
    if fw.dmar.is_none() && fw.ivrs.is_none() {
        if fw.unreadable.is_none() && x86 {
            f.push(
                Finding::new("DMA-012", Severity::High, "Firmware exposes no IOMMU (no ACPI DMAR / IVRS table)")
                    .detail("VT-d / AMD-Vi is disabled or unsupported, so every PCIe, Thunderbolt and FireWire device can read and write all of physical memory (PCILeech-style attacks, malicious peripherals).")
                    .fix("Enable 'VT-d' / 'Intel Virtualization for Directed I/O' or 'IOMMU' / 'AMD-Vi' in firmware setup.")
                    .source("acpi/DMAR"),
            );
        } else if let Some(e) = &fw.unreadable {
            f.push(
                Finding::new(
                    "DMA-015",
                    Severity::Info,
                    "ACPI DMAR/IVRS tables not readable",
                )
                .detail(e.clone())
                .fix("Re-run as root to include firmware-table checks."),
            );
        }
        return f;
    }
    if let Some(d) = &fw.dmar {
        if !d.dma_ctrl_platform_opt_in {
            f.push(
                Finding::new("DMA-003", Severity::Medium, "Firmware does not opt in to pre-boot DMA protection (DMAR)")
                    .detail("DMA_CTRL_PLATFORM_OPT_IN is clear: firmware does not promise to keep VT-d protecting memory across the boot-to-OS handoff. Windows Kernel DMA Protection and Linux Thunderbolt `iommu_dma_protection` stay off on such platforms, and devices can DMA during early boot.")
                    .fix("Update firmware; enable 'Pre-boot DMA protection' / 'Kernel DMA Protection' / 'Thunderbolt DMA protection' in setup if offered.")
                    .source("acpi/DMAR"),
            );
        }
        if !d.intr_remap {
            f.push(
                Finding::new("DMA-007", Severity::Medium, "Interrupt remapping not supported (DMAR)")
                    .detail("Without interrupt remapping a DMA-capable device can forge MSIs and inject interrupts, a known IOMMU bypass.")
                    .fix("Enable interrupt remapping / x2APIC in firmware or update it.")
                    .source("acpi/DMAR"),
            );
        }
        if d.x2apic_opt_out {
            f.push(
                Finding::new("DMA-014", Severity::Low, "Firmware requests x2APIC opt-out")
                    .detail("X2APIC_OPT_OUT asks the OS to stay in xAPIC mode, which limits interrupt-remapping protection.")
                    .source("acpi/DMAR"),
            );
        }
        let odd: Vec<String> = d
            .rmrrs
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|r| {
                r.devices
                    .iter()
                    .map(move |dev| format!("{dev} [{}..{}]", r.base, r.limit))
            })
            .filter(|dev| {
                !dev.contains("00:02.0")
                    && !dev.contains("00:14.0")
                    && !dev.contains("00:1a.")
                    && !dev.contains("00:1d.")
            })
            .collect();
        if !odd.is_empty() {
            let mut fi = Finding::new("DMA-010", Severity::Info, format!("{} RMRR identity-mapped region(s) on non-legacy devices", odd.len()))
                .detail("Reserved Memory Region Reporting forces identity mappings that the IOMMU cannot fully isolate. Expected for integrated graphics/USB; unusual elsewhere.")
                .source("acpi/DMAR");
            for o in odd.into_iter().take(10) {
                fi = fi.evidence(o);
            }
            f.push(fi);
        }
        if !d.header.checksum_ok {
            f.push(
                Finding::new("DMA-011", Severity::Low, "DMAR table checksum is invalid")
                    .detail("Firmware bug or tampered table.")
                    .source("acpi/DMAR"),
            );
        }
    }
    if let Some(v) = &fw.ivrs {
        if !v.dma_remap_opt_in {
            f.push(
                Finding::new("DMA-003", Severity::Medium, "Firmware does not opt in to pre-boot DMA protection (IVRS)")
                    .detail("IVinfo DMA-remap bit clear: the AMD platform does not request DMA protection through boot, so OS-level Kernel DMA Protection stays off.")
                    .fix("Update firmware; enable 'Kernel DMA Protection' / 'DMA protection' in setup if offered.")
                    .source("acpi/IVRS"),
            );
        }
        if !v.header.checksum_ok {
            f.push(
                Finding::new("DMA-011", Severity::Low, "IVRS table checksum is invalid")
                    .detail("Firmware bug or tampered table.")
                    .source("acpi/IVRS"),
            );
        }
    }
    f
}

#[cfg(not(windows))]
pub fn linux(s: &crate::linux::LinuxState) -> Vec<Finding> {
    use crate::linux::has_arg;
    let mut f = Vec::new();
    let cmd = s.cmdline.as_deref().unwrap_or("");

    for arg in ["intel_iommu=off", "amd_iommu=off", "iommu=off"] {
        if has_arg(cmd, arg) {
            f.push(
                Finding::new("DMA-006", Severity::High, format!("IOMMU disabled on the kernel command line ({arg})"))
                    .detail("The kernel was told not to use the IOMMU; every bus-mastering device has unrestricted access to RAM.")
                    .fix(format!("Remove `{arg}` from the bootloader configuration."))
                    .source("/proc/cmdline"),
            );
        }
    }
    if s.iommu_units.is_empty() && !s.wsl {
        f.push(
            Finding::new("DMA-001", Severity::High, "No IOMMU is active")
                .detail("/sys/class/iommu is empty: devices are not isolated from system memory.")
                .fix("Enable VT-d / AMD-Vi in firmware; on Intel with older kernels add intel_iommu=on.")
                .source("/sys/class/iommu"),
        );
    }
    let identity = s.domain_types.get("identity").copied().unwrap_or(0);
    if identity > 0 || has_arg(cmd, "iommu=pt") || has_arg(cmd, "iommu.passthrough=1") {
        f.push(
            Finding::new("DMA-002", Severity::Medium, format!("IOMMU in passthrough mode ({identity} identity-mapped group(s))"))
                .detail("Identity domains give devices 1:1 access to physical memory — the IOMMU is present but not isolating them. Thunderbolt/untrusted devices are still forced into DMA domains, internal ones are not.")
                .fix("Drop iommu=pt / iommu.passthrough=1 unless required for performance; prefer iommu.strict=1.")
                .source("/sys/kernel/iommu_groups/*/type"),
        );
    }
    if let Some(n) = s.domain_types.get("DMA-FQ").filter(|n| **n > 0) {
        f.push(
            Finding::new("DMA-016", Severity::Low, format!("Lazy IOTLB invalidation on {n} group(s) (DMA-FQ)"))
                .detail("Flush queues defer IOTLB invalidation, leaving a short window where a device can still reach freed buffers.")
                .fix("Boot with iommu.strict=1 on machines exposed to untrusted peripherals.")
                .source("/sys/kernel/iommu_groups/*/type"),
        );
    }
    for d in &s.thunderbolt {
        let src = format!("/sys/bus/thunderbolt/devices/{}/security", d.name);
        match d.security.as_str() {
            "none" if d.iommu_dma_protection != Some(true) => f.push(
                Finding::new("DMA-005", Severity::High, format!("Thunderbolt {} security level 'none' without DMA protection", d.name))
                    .detail("Any Thunderbolt device is connected automatically with PCIe tunnelling and no IOMMU backstop — a plug-in DMA attack needs no user interaction.")
                    .fix("Set the Thunderbolt security level to 'user' or 'secure' in firmware (and use bolt/boltctl to authorise devices), or enable Kernel DMA Protection.")
                    .source(src),
            ),
            "none" => f.push(
                Finding::new("DMA-005", Severity::Low, format!("Thunderbolt {} security level 'none' (IOMMU-protected)", d.name))
                    .detail("Devices auto-connect, but iommu_dma_protection=1 confines them to their own DMA domains.")
                    .source(src),
            ),
            _ => {}
        }
        if d.iommu_dma_protection == Some(false) && d.security != "none" {
            f.push(
                Finding::new("DMA-004", Severity::Medium, format!("Thunderbolt {}: iommu_dma_protection off", d.name))
                    .detail("Authorised Thunderbolt devices are not confined by the IOMMU (requires firmware DMA opt-in + IOMMU).")
                    .fix("Enable the IOMMU and firmware pre-boot DMA protection.")
                    .source(format!("/sys/bus/thunderbolt/devices/{}/iommu_dma_protection", d.name)),
            );
        }
    }
    if !s.removable_pci.is_empty() {
        let mut fi = Finding::new(
            "DMA-013",
            Severity::Info,
            format!(
                "{} external (removable) PCIe device(s) attached",
                s.removable_pci.len()
            ),
        )
        .detail("Devices behind external-facing ports; confirm each one is expected.")
        .source("/sys/bus/pci/devices/*/removable");
        for p in &s.removable_pci {
            fi = fi.evidence(format!(
                "{} {}:{} class {} group {}",
                p.address,
                p.vendor,
                p.device,
                p.class,
                p.iommu_group.as_deref().unwrap_or("-")
            ));
        }
        f.push(fi);
    }
    if s.firewire {
        f.push(
            Finding::new("DMA-009", Severity::Low, "FireWire (IEEE 1394) controller active")
                .detail("FireWire's physical DMA (SBP-2) is the original DMA attack vector; it relies on the IOMMU and firewire-ohci filtering.")
                .fix("Blacklist firewire_ohci / firewire_sbp2 if unused, or disable the controller in firmware.")
                .source("/sys/module/firewire_ohci"),
        );
    }
    f
}

#[cfg(windows)]
pub fn windows(s: &crate::windows::WinState) -> Vec<Finding> {
    let mut f = Vec::new();
    if s.iommu_available == Some(false) {
        f.push(
            Finding::new("DMA-001", Severity::High, "No IOMMU available to Windows")
                .detail("Neither the hypervisor nor the kernel can isolate device DMA: every PCIe/Thunderbolt device can read all of memory.")
                .fix("Enable VT-d / AMD IOMMU (AMD-Vi) in firmware setup.")
                .source("ntdll!NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemVsmProtectionInformation)"),
        );
    }
    if s.kernel_dma_protection == Some(false) {
        let iommu_ok = s.iommu_available == Some(true);
        f.push(
            Finding::new("DMA-004", if iommu_ok { Severity::Medium } else { Severity::High }, "Kernel DMA Protection is off")
                .detail(if iommu_ok {
                    "The IOMMU works (VBS uses it), but Windows does not confine external PCIe / Thunderbolt / USB4 devices. This almost always means firmware lacks the pre-boot DMA opt-in flag (see DMA-003), so a hot-plugged device can DMA into memory — including on the lock screen."
                } else {
                    "External PCIe / Thunderbolt / USB4 devices are not confined by an IOMMU."
                })
                .fix("Update firmware and enable 'Kernel DMA Protection' / 'Pre-boot DMA protection' in setup. Until then: BitLocker with pre-boot PIN, and disable external PCIe tunnelling (Thunderbolt/USB4 PCIe) in firmware when unused.")
                .source("ntdll!NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemDmaGuardPolicyInformation)"),
        );
    }
    let src =
        r"HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Kernel DMA Protection\DeviceEnumerationPolicy";
    match s.enumeration_policy {
        Some(2) => f.push(
            Finding::new("DMA-008", Severity::Medium, "DMA enumeration policy allows all external devices")
                .detail("DeviceEnumerationPolicy=2 lets external devices incompatible with DMA remapping start at any time, even on the lock screen.")
                .fix("Set the Group Policy 'Enumeration policy for external devices incompatible with Kernel DMA Protection' to 'Block all' (0).")
                .source(src),
        ),
        Some(1) | None if s.kernel_dma_protection == Some(true) => f.push(
            Finding::new("DMA-008", Severity::Info, "Incompatible external devices enumerate after user sign-in (default)")
                .detail("Default policy: devices that do not support DMA remapping are blocked only until a user logs in.")
                .fix("Set the policy to 'Block all' (0) for high-risk machines.")
                .source(src),
        ),
        _ => {}
    }
    f
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::acpi::{build, parse_dmar};

    #[test]
    fn missing_tables_is_high_unless_unreadable() {
        let f = firmware(&Firmware::default(), true);
        assert_eq!(f[0].id, "DMA-012");
        let f = firmware(
            &Firmware {
                unreadable: Some("root".into()),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            true,
        );
        assert_eq!(f[0].id, "DMA-015");
    }

    #[test]
    fn dmar_without_opt_in_flags() {
        let fw = Firmware {
            dmar: parse_dmar(&build::dmar(0b001, true)),
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let ids: Vec<&str> = firmware(&fw, true).iter().map(|f| f.id).collect();
        assert_eq!(ids, vec!["DMA-003"]); // xHCI RMRR is expected, not reported
        let fw = Firmware {
            dmar: parse_dmar(&build::dmar(0b101, false)),
            ..Default::default()
        };
        assert!(firmware(&fw, true).is_empty());
    }
}

```rs
//! Linux DMA surface: IOMMU units and domain types, boot parameters,
//! Thunderbolt security, external-facing PCIe and FireWire.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use serde::Serialize;

#[derive(Debug, Default, Serialize)]
pub struct TbDomain {
    pub name: String,
    pub security: String,
    pub iommu_dma_protection: Option<bool>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Default, Serialize)]
pub struct TbDevice {
    pub id: String,
    pub vendor: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub authorized: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Default, Serialize)]
pub struct PciDev {
    pub address: String,
    pub vendor: String,
    pub device: String,
    pub class: String,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub iommu_group: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Default, Serialize)]
pub struct LinuxState {
    pub iommu_units: Vec<String>,
    pub iommu_groups: usize,
    /// Default domain type per group: DMA, DMA-FQ, identity, unmanaged, blocked.
    pub domain_types: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, usize>,
    pub cmdline: Option<String>,
    pub thunderbolt: Vec<TbDomain>,
    pub tb_devices: Vec<TbDevice>,
    pub removable_pci: Vec<PciDev>,
    pub firewire: bool,
    #[serde(skip)]
    pub dmar_raw: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    #[serde(skip)]
    pub ivrs_raw: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    #[serde(skip)]
    pub acpi_error: Option<String>,
    pub wsl: bool,
}

fn rd(root: &Path, p: &str) -> Option<String> {
    std::fs::read_to_string(root.join(p.trim_start_matches('/')))
        .ok()
        .map(|s| s.trim().to_string())
}

fn entries(dir: PathBuf) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    let mut v: Vec<PathBuf> = std::fs::read_dir(dir)
        .into_iter()
        .flatten()
        .flatten()
        .map(|e| e.path())
        .collect();
    v.sort();
    v
}

fn name(p: &Path) -> String {
    p.file_name()
        .map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

fn read_table(root: &Path, sig: &str, state_err: &mut Option<String>) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    let p = root.join("sys/firmware/acpi/tables").join(sig);
    match std::fs::read(&p) {
        Ok(b) => Some(b),
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied => {
            *state_err = Some(format!("{} needs root", p.display()));
            None
        }
        Err(_) => None,
    }
}

pub fn collect(root: &Path) -> LinuxState {
    let mut s = LinuxState {
        cmdline: rd(root, "/proc/cmdline"),
        wsl: rd(root, "/proc/sys/kernel/osrelease")
            .is_some_and(|r| r.to_ascii_lowercase().contains("microsoft")),
        ..Default::default()
    };
    s.iommu_units = entries(root.join("sys/class/iommu"))
        .iter()
        .map(|p| name(p))
        .collect();
    let groups = entries(root.join("sys/kernel/iommu_groups"));
    s.iommu_groups = groups.len();
    for g in &groups {
        if let Ok(t) = std::fs::read_to_string(g.join("type")) {
            *s.domain_types.entry(t.trim().to_string()).or_default() += 1;
        }
    }

    for d in entries(root.join("sys/bus/thunderbolt/devices")) {
        let n = name(&d);
        if n.starts_with("domain") {
            s.thunderbolt.push(TbDomain {
                security: std::fs::read_to_string(d.join("security"))
                    .map(|v| v.trim().to_string())
                    .unwrap_or_default(),
                iommu_dma_protection: std::fs::read_to_string(d.join("iommu_dma_protection"))
                    .ok()
                    .map(|v| v.trim() == "1"),
                name: n,
            });
        } else if n.contains('-') && !n.contains(':') && !n.ends_with("-0") {
            let r = |f: &str| {
                std::fs::read_to_string(d.join(f))
                    .map(|v| v.trim().to_string())
                    .ok()
            };
            s.tb_devices.push(TbDevice {
                vendor: r("vendor_name").unwrap_or_default(),
                name: r("device_name").unwrap_or_default(),
                authorized: r("authorized"),
                id: n,
            });
        }
    }

    for d in entries(root.join("sys/bus/pci/devices")) {
        let r = |f: &str| {
            std::fs::read_to_string(d.join(f))
                .map(|v| v.trim().to_string())
                .ok()
        };
        if r("removable").as_deref() == Some("removable") {
            s.removable_pci.push(PciDev {
                // uevent carries the canonical address; the directory name is
                // the same on a live system but may differ in snapshots.
                address: r("uevent")
                    .and_then(|u| {
                        u.lines()
                            .find_map(|l| l.strip_prefix("PCI_SLOT_NAME=").map(str::to_string))
                    })
                    .unwrap_or_else(|| name(&d)),
                vendor: r("vendor").unwrap_or_default(),
                device: r("device").unwrap_or_default(),
                class: r("class").unwrap_or_default(),
                iommu_group: std::fs::read_link(d.join("iommu_group"))
                    .ok()
                    .map(|l| name(&l)),
            });
        }
    }

    s.firewire = root.join("sys/module/firewire_ohci").exists()
        || !entries(root.join("sys/bus/firewire/devices")).is_empty();
    let mut err = None;
    s.dmar_raw = read_table(root, "DMAR", &mut err);
    s.ivrs_raw = read_table(root, "IVRS", &mut err);
    s.acpi_error = err;
    s
}

pub fn has_arg(cmdline: &str, arg: &str) -> bool {
    cmdline
        .split_whitespace()
        .any(|a| a == arg || (arg.ends_with('=') && a.starts_with(arg)))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn collects_fixture() {
        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("dmaguard-fx-{}", std::process::id()));
        let w = |p: &str, v: &str| {
            let f = root.join(p);
            std::fs::create_dir_all(f.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
            std::fs::write(f, v).unwrap();
        };
        w("proc/cmdline", "root=/dev/nvme0n1p2 iommu=pt\n");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(root.join("sys/class/iommu/dmar0")).unwrap();
        w("sys/kernel/iommu_groups/0/type", "identity\n");
        w("sys/kernel/iommu_groups/1/type", "DMA-FQ\n");
        w("sys/bus/thunderbolt/devices/domain0/security", "none\n");
        w(
            "sys/bus/thunderbolt/devices/domain0/iommu_dma_protection",
            "0\n",
        );
        w("sys/bus/thunderbolt/devices/0-1/vendor_name", "Dock Co\n");
        w("sys/bus/thunderbolt/devices/0-1/authorized", "1\n");
        w("sys/bus/pci/devices/ext0/removable", "removable\n");
        w("sys/bus/pci/devices/ext0/vendor", "0x8086\n");
        w(
            "sys/bus/pci/devices/ext0/uevent",
            "PCI_SLOT_NAME=0000:05:00.0\n",
        );
        let s = collect(&root);
        assert_eq!(s.iommu_units, vec!["dmar0"]);
        assert_eq!(s.iommu_groups, 2);
        assert_eq!(s.domain_types.get("identity"), Some(&1));
        assert_eq!(s.thunderbolt[0].security, "none");
        assert_eq!(s.thunderbolt[0].iommu_dma_protection, Some(false));
        assert_eq!(s.tb_devices.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(s.removable_pci[0].address, "0000:05:00.0");
        assert!(has_arg(s.cmdline.as_deref().unwrap(), "iommu=pt"));
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(root).ok();
    }
}

`src/main.rs`:

```rs
//! dmaguard — read-only DMA attack-surface auditor.
//!
//! Answers "can a device I plug in read my memory?": parses the firmware's
//! ACPI DMAR (Intel VT-d) / IVRS (AMD-Vi) tables, then checks how the OS uses
//! the IOMMU — Kernel DMA Protection on Windows; IOMMU domains, boot
//! parameters, Thunderbolt security and external PCIe on Linux.

mod acpi;
mod checks;
#[cfg(not(windows))]
mod linux;
mod report;
#[cfg(windows)]
mod windows;

use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::process::ExitCode;

use anstream::println;
use clap::Parser;
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
use serde_json::json;

use checks::Firmware;
use report::{Finding, Severity};

const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");
const REPO: &str = "https://github.com/grimh3xx/dmaguard";

#[derive(Parser)]
#[command(
    name = "dmaguard",
    version,
    about = "Read-only DMA / IOMMU attack-surface auditor"
)]
struct Cli {
    /// Parse this raw ACPI DMAR table instead of the system's
    #[arg(long, value_name = "FILE")]
    dmar: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// Parse this raw ACPI IVRS table instead of the system's
    #[arg(long, value_name = "FILE")]
    ivrs: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// Linux: audit a tree rooted here (snapshot of /proc and /sys)
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    #[arg(long, value_name = "DIR")]
    root: Option<PathBuf>,
    #[arg(long, conflicts_with = "sarif")]
    json: bool,
    #[arg(long)]
    sarif: bool,
    #[arg(long, default_value = "info", value_name = "LVL")]
    min_severity: String,
    #[arg(long)]
    no_color: bool,
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let cli = Cli::parse();
    if cli.no_color {
        anstream::ColorChoice::Never.write_global();
    }
    let Some(min) = Severity::parse(&cli.min_severity) else {
        eprintln!("invalid --min-severity: {}", cli.min_severity);
        return ExitCode::from(64);
    };
    let x86 = cfg!(any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "x86"));

    let (os_state, mut dmar_raw, mut ivrs_raw, unreadable, os_findings, not_applicable) =
        gather(&cli);
    if let Some(p) = &cli.dmar {
        dmar_raw = std::fs::read(p).ok();
    }
    if let Some(p) = &cli.ivrs {
        ivrs_raw = std::fs::read(p).ok();
    }
    let fw = Firmware {
        dmar: dmar_raw.as_deref().and_then(acpi::parse_dmar),
        ivrs: ivrs_raw.as_deref().and_then(acpi::parse_ivrs),
        unreadable: if cli.dmar.is_some() || cli.ivrs.is_some() {
            None
        } else {
            unreadable
        },
    };

    let mut findings: Vec<Finding> = Vec::new();
    if not_applicable {
        findings.push(
            Finding::new(
                "DMA-017",
                Severity::Info,
                "Running inside WSL — host DMA protection is not visible",
            )
            .detail("The WSL2 VM has no physical devices; the Windows host owns the IOMMU.")
            .fix("Run dmaguard.exe on the Windows host."),
        );
    } else {
        findings.extend(checks::firmware(&fw, x86));
        findings.extend(os_findings);
    }
    let findings = report::filter_sort(findings, min);

    if cli.json {
        let v = json!({ "tool": "dmaguard", "version": VERSION, "firmware": fw, "os": os_state, "findings": findings });
        println!(
            "{}",
            serde_json::to_string_pretty(&v).expect("serializable")
        );
    } else if cli.sarif {
        let s = report::sarif("dmaguard", VERSION, REPO, "platform/dma", &findings);
        println!(
            "{}",
            serde_json::to_string_pretty(&s).expect("serializable")
        );
    } else {
        banner();
        render_firmware(&fw);
        render_os(&os_state);
        report::print_findings(&findings);
        report::print_summary(&findings);
        println!();
    }
    ExitCode::from(report::worst(&findings))
}

type Gathered = (
    serde_json::Value,
    Option<Vec<u8>>,
    Option<Vec<u8>>,
    Option<String>,
    Vec<Finding>,
    bool,
);

#[cfg(not(windows))]
fn gather(cli: &Cli) -> Gathered {
    let root = cli.root.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("/"));
    let mut s = linux::collect(&root);
    let f = checks::linux(&s);
    let (d, i) = (s.dmar_raw.take(), s.ivrs_raw.take());
    let wsl = s.wsl && cli.root.is_none() && cli.dmar.is_none() && cli.ivrs.is_none();
    (
        serde_json::to_value(&s).expect("serializable"),
        d,
        i,
        s.acpi_error.clone(),
        f,
        wsl,
    )
}

#[cfg(windows)]
fn gather(_cli: &Cli) -> Gathered {
    let mut s = windows::collect();
    let f = checks::windows(&s);
    let (d, i) = (s.dmar_raw.take(), s.ivrs_raw.take());
    (
        serde_json::to_value(&s).expect("serializable"),
        d,
        i,
        None,
        f,
        false,
    )
}

fn banner() {
    println!();
    println!(
        "  {}{}  {}",
        "dma".bold().cyan(),
        "guard".bold().bright_blue(),
        format!("v{VERSION}").dimmed()
    );
    println!(
        "  {}",
        "DMA / IOMMU attack-surface auditor · read-only".dimmed()
    );
}

fn flag(b: bool) -> String {
    if b {
        "yes".green().to_string()
    } else {
        "no".red().to_string()
    }
}

fn render_firmware(fw: &Firmware) {
    report::section("firmware (ACPI)");
    match &fw.dmar {
        Some(d) => {
            report::kv(
                "DMAR",
                format!(
                    "{} {} rev {}{}",
                    d.header.oem_id,
                    d.header.oem_table_id,
                    d.header.revision,
                    if d.header.checksum_ok {
                        ""
                    } else {
                        " (bad checksum)"
                    }
                ),
            );
            report::kv(
                "  remapping units",
                format!(
                    "{} DRHD{}",
                    d.drhd_units,
                    if d.include_pci_all {
                        " (INCLUDE_PCI_ALL)"
                    } else {
                        ""
                    }
                ),
            );
            report::kv("  address width", format!("{} bits", d.host_address_width));
            report::kv("  DMA opt-in", flag(d.dma_ctrl_platform_opt_in));
            report::kv("  interrupt remap", flag(d.intr_remap));
            report::kv(
                "  RMRR / ATSR / SATC",
                format!("{} / {} / {}", d.rmrrs.len(), d.atsr, d.satc),
            );
        }
        None => report::kv("DMAR", "—".dimmed()),
    }
    match &fw.ivrs {
        Some(v) => {
            report::kv(
                "IVRS",
                format!(
                    "{} {} rev {}",
                    v.header.oem_id, v.header.oem_table_id, v.header.revision
                ),
            );
            report::kv(
                "  IVHD / IVMD",
                format!("{} / {}", v.ivhd_blocks, v.ivmd_blocks),
            );
            report::kv("  DMA remap opt-in", flag(v.dma_remap_opt_in));
        }
        None => report::kv("IVRS", "—".dimmed()),
    }
    if let Some(e) = &fw.unreadable {
        report::kv("note", e.yellow());
    }
}

/// One-line rendering of a JSON value: strings bare, objects as `k=v`.
fn compact(v: &serde_json::Value) -> String {
    match v {
        serde_json::Value::String(t) => t.clone(),
        serde_json::Value::Object(o) => o
            .iter()
            .filter(|(_, x)| !x.is_null())
            .map(|(k, x)| format!("{k}={}", compact(x)))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join(" "),
        other => other.to_string(),
    }
}

fn render_os(s: &serde_json::Value) {
    report::section("operating system");
    let Some(obj) = s.as_object() else { return };
    for (k, v) in obj {
        let shown = match v {
            serde_json::Value::Null => continue,
            serde_json::Value::Bool(b) => flag(*b),
            serde_json::Value::Array(a) if a.is_empty() => "none".dimmed().to_string(),
            serde_json::Value::Array(a) => a.iter().map(compact).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" | "),
            serde_json::Value::Object(o) if o.is_empty() => "—".dimmed().to_string(),
            serde_json::Value::Object(o) => o
                .iter()
                .map(|(a, b)| format!("{a}={b}"))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join(" "),
            serde_json::Value::String(t) => t.clone(),
            other => other.to_string(),
        };
        report::kv(&k.replace('_', " "), shown);
    }
}

```rs
//! Findings model and the three output channels shared by every grimh3xx
//! auditor: colored terminal, JSON, and SARIF 2.1.0 (GitHub code scanning).
//!
//! The exit code is the worst severity *shown* (0 none/info .. 4 critical) so
//! the tool can gate a CI job or a fleet-compliance script directly.

use anstream::println;
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::{json, Value};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Severity {
    Info,
    Low,
    Medium,
    High,
    Critical,
}

impl Severity {
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        match s.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
            "info" | "none" => Some(Self::Info),
            "low" => Some(Self::Low),
            "medium" | "med" => Some(Self::Medium),
            "high" => Some(Self::High),
            "critical" | "crit" => Some(Self::Critical),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Info => "INFO",
            Self::Low => "LOW",
            Self::Medium => "MEDIUM",
            Self::High => "HIGH",
            Self::Critical => "CRITICAL",
        }
    }

    pub fn exit_code(self) -> u8 {
        self as u8
    }

    fn sarif_level(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Critical | Self::High => "error",
            Self::Medium => "warning",
            Self::Low | Self::Info => "note",
        }
    }

    /// CVSS-like numeric hint GitHub uses to bucket `security-severity`.
    fn security_severity(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Critical => "9.5",
            Self::High => "8.0",
            Self::Medium => "5.5",
            Self::Low => "3.0",
            Self::Info => "0.0",
        }
    }

    fn painted(self) -> String {
        let tag = format!("{:<8}", self.label());
        match self {
            Self::Critical => tag.on_red().white().bold().to_string(),
            Self::High => tag.red().bold().to_string(),
            Self::Medium => tag.yellow().bold().to_string(),
            Self::Low => tag.cyan().to_string(),
            Self::Info => tag.dimmed().to_string(),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize)]
pub struct Finding {
    pub id: &'static str,
    pub severity: Severity,
    pub title: String,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "String::is_empty")]
    pub detail: String,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "String::is_empty")]
    pub remediation: String,
    /// Where the evidence came from (a sysfs node, a registry value, a file).
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub source: Option<String>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    pub evidence: Vec<String>,
}

impl Finding {
    pub fn new(id: &'static str, severity: Severity, title: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            id,
            severity,
            title: title.into(),
            detail: String::new(),
            remediation: String::new(),
            source: None,
            evidence: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn detail(mut self, d: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.detail = d.into();
        self
    }

    pub fn fix(mut self, r: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.remediation = r.into();
        self
    }

    pub fn source(mut self, s: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.source = Some(s.into());
        self
    }

    pub fn evidence(mut self, e: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.evidence.push(e.into());
        self
    }
}

/// Keep findings at or above `min`, most severe first, stable by id.
pub fn filter_sort(mut findings: Vec<Finding>, min: Severity) -> Vec<Finding> {
    findings.retain(|f| f.severity >= min);
    findings.sort_by(|a, b| b.severity.cmp(&a.severity).then(a.id.cmp(b.id)));
    findings
}

pub fn worst(findings: &[Finding]) -> u8 {
    findings
        .iter()
        .map(|f| f.severity.exit_code())
        .max()
        .unwrap_or(0)
}

pub fn section(title: &str) {
    println!();
    println!("  {} {}", "▌".cyan(), title.bold());
}

pub fn kv(key: &str, value: impl std::fmt::Display) {
    println!("    {:<26} {}", key.dimmed(), value);
}

pub fn print_findings(findings: &[Finding]) {
    section("findings");
    if findings.is_empty() {
        println!("    {}", "no findings at the selected severity".green());
        return;
    }
    for f in findings {
        println!();
        println!(
            "    {} {}  {}",
            f.severity.painted(),
            f.id.bright_blue(),
            f.title.bold()
        );
        if !f.detail.is_empty() {
            for line in wrap(&f.detail, 86) {
                println!("             {}", line);
            }
        }
        for e in &f.evidence {
            println!("             {} {}", "·".dimmed(), e.dimmed());
        }
        if let Some(src) = &f.source {
            println!("             {} {}", "src".dimmed(), src.dimmed());
        }
        if !f.remediation.is_empty() {
            let mut lines = wrap(&f.remediation, 80).into_iter();
            if let Some(first) = lines.next() {
                println!("             {} {}", "fix".green(), first);
            }
            for line in lines {
                println!("                 {}", line);
            }
        }
    }
}

pub fn print_summary(findings: &[Finding]) {
    let count = |s: Severity| findings.iter().filter(|f| f.severity == s).count();
    println!();
    println!(
        "  {} {} critical · {} high · {} medium · {} low · {} info",
        "Σ".cyan().bold(),
        count(Severity::Critical).red().bold(),
        count(Severity::High).red(),
        count(Severity::Medium).yellow(),
        count(Severity::Low).cyan(),
        count(Severity::Info).dimmed(),
    );
}

fn wrap(text: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for para in text.split('\n') {
        let mut line = String::new();
        for word in para.split_whitespace() {
            if !line.is_empty() && line.chars().count() + 1 + word.chars().count() > width {
                out.push(std::mem::take(&mut line));
            }
            if !line.is_empty() {
                line.push(' ');
            }
            line.push_str(word);
        }
        out.push(line);
    }
    out
}

/// SARIF 2.1.0 log. Host-level findings have no source file, so the evidence
/// source (or `fallback_uri`) is used as the artifact location; GitHub code
/// scanning rejects results without a location.
pub fn sarif(
    tool: &str,
    version: &str,
    info_uri: &str,
    fallback_uri: &str,
    findings: &[Finding],
) -> Value {
    let mut rule_ids: Vec<&str> = findings.iter().map(|f| f.id).collect();
    rule_ids.sort_unstable();
    rule_ids.dedup();

    let rules: Vec<Value> = rule_ids
        .iter()
        .map(|id| {
            let f = findings.iter().find(|f| f.id == *id).expect("rule from findings");
            json!({
                "id": id,
                "name": id.replace('-', ""),
                "shortDescription": { "text": f.title },
                "help": { "text": if f.remediation.is_empty() { f.title.clone() } else { f.remediation.clone() } },
                "properties": {
                    "security-severity": f.severity.security_severity(),
                    "tags": ["security", "hardening"],
                },
            })
        })
        .collect();

    let results: Vec<Value> = findings
        .iter()
        .map(|f| {
            let uri = f
                .source
                .as_deref()
                .unwrap_or(fallback_uri)
                .trim_start_matches('/')
                .replace('\\', "/");
            let mut text = f.title.clone();
            if !f.detail.is_empty() {
                text.push_str(" — ");
                text.push_str(&f.detail);
            }
            json!({
                "ruleId": f.id,
                "level": f.severity.sarif_level(),
                "message": { "text": text },
                "locations": [{
                    "physicalLocation": { "artifactLocation": { "uri": uri } }
                }],
                "properties": { "severity": f.severity, "evidence": f.evidence },
            })
        })
        .collect();

    json!({
        "$schema": "https://json.schemastore.org/sarif-2.1.0.json",
        "version": "2.1.0",
        "runs": [{
            "tool": { "driver": {
                "name": tool,
                "version": version,
                "informationUri": info_uri,
                "rules": rules,
            }},
            "results": results,
        }],
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn worst_is_max_severity() {
        let f = vec![
            Finding::new("A-1", Severity::Low, "a"),
            Finding::new("A-2", Severity::High, "b"),
        ];
        assert_eq!(worst(&f), 3);
        assert_eq!(worst(&[]), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn filter_drops_and_sorts() {
        let f = vec![
            Finding::new("B", Severity::Info, "i"),
            Finding::new("A", Severity::Medium, "m"),
            Finding::new("C", Severity::Critical, "c"),
        ];
        let out = filter_sort(f, Severity::Medium);
        assert_eq!(out.iter().map(|f| f.id).collect::<Vec<_>>(), ["C", "A"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn sarif_has_location_for_every_result() {
        let f = vec![Finding::new("X-1", Severity::High, "t").source("/sys/x")];
        let s = sarif("t", "0", "u", "host", &f);
        assert_eq!(
            s["runs"][0]["results"][0]["locations"][0]["physicalLocation"]["artifactLocation"]
                ["uri"],
            "sys/x"
        );
        assert_eq!(s["runs"][0]["results"][0]["level"], "error");
    }
}

//! Windows DMA surface: Kernel DMA Protection state straight from the kernel,
//! the device-enumeration policy, and the ACPI DMAR/IVRS tables.

use serde::Serialize;
use windows_sys::Wdk::System::SystemInformation::NtQuerySystemInformation;
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Registry::{RegGetValueW, HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE, RRF_RT_REG_DWORD};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::SystemInformation::GetSystemFirmwareTable;

/// SYSTEM_VSM_PROTECTION_INFORMATION { DmaProtectionsAvailable,
/// DmaProtectionsInUse, HardwareMbecAvailable, ApicVirtualizationAvailable }.
/// This is the IOMMU as used by the hypervisor/VBS — *not* Kernel DMA
/// Protection: it can read 1/1 while external devices are unprotected.
const SYSTEM_VSM_PROTECTION_INFORMATION: i32 = 169;
/// SYSTEM_DMA_GUARD_POLICY_INFORMATION { DmaGuardPolicyEnabled } — what
/// msinfo32 reports as "Kernel DMA Protection". Requires a 1-byte buffer.
const SYSTEM_DMA_GUARD_POLICY_INFORMATION: i32 = 202;

#[derive(Debug, Default, Serialize)]
pub struct WinState {
    /// IOMMU available to / used by the hypervisor (VBS).
    pub iommu_available: Option<bool>,
    pub iommu_in_use_by_vbs: Option<bool>,
    /// Kernel DMA Protection for external devices.
    pub kernel_dma_protection: Option<bool>,
    pub mbec_available: Option<bool>,
    /// HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Kernel DMA Protection\DeviceEnumerationPolicy
    pub enumeration_policy: Option<u32>,
    #[serde(skip)]
    pub dmar_raw: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    #[serde(skip)]
    pub ivrs_raw: Option<Vec<u8>>,
}

fn query(class: i32, len: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut b = vec![0u8; len];
    let mut ret = 0u32;
    // SAFETY: b is writable for `len` bytes.
    let st =
        unsafe { NtQuerySystemInformation(class, b.as_mut_ptr().cast(), len as u32, &mut ret) };
    (st >= 0).then_some(b)
}

fn acpi_table(sig: &[u8; 4]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    let provider = u32::from_be_bytes(*b"ACPI");
    let id = u32::from_le_bytes(*sig);
    // SAFETY: size query with a null buffer, then a fill of exactly that size.
    unsafe {
        let n = GetSystemFirmwareTable(provider, id, std::ptr::null_mut(), 0);
        if n == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let mut b = vec![0u8; n as usize];
        let got = GetSystemFirmwareTable(provider, id, b.as_mut_ptr().cast(), n);
        (got == n).then_some(b)
    }
}

fn reg_dword(key: &str, value: &str) -> Option<u32> {
    let w = |s: &str| s.encode_utf16().chain(Some(0)).collect::<Vec<u16>>();
    let (k, v) = (w(key), w(value));
    let mut data = 0u32;
    let mut size = 4u32;
    // SAFETY: 4-byte out buffer; NUL-terminated strings.
    let rc = unsafe {
        RegGetValueW(
            HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE,
            k.as_ptr(),
            v.as_ptr(),
            RRF_RT_REG_DWORD,
            std::ptr::null_mut(),
            (&mut data as *mut u32).cast(),
            &mut size,
        )
    };
    (rc == 0).then_some(data)
}

pub fn collect() -> WinState {
    let vsm = query(SYSTEM_VSM_PROTECTION_INFORMATION, 4);
    WinState {
        iommu_available: vsm.as_ref().map(|b| b[0] != 0),
        iommu_in_use_by_vbs: vsm.as_ref().map(|b| b[1] != 0),
        mbec_available: vsm.as_ref().map(|b| b[2] != 0),
        kernel_dma_protection: query(SYSTEM_DMA_GUARD_POLICY_INFORMATION, 1).map(|b| b[0] != 0),
        enumeration_policy: reg_dword(
            r"SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Kernel DMA Protection",
            "DeviceEnumerationPolicy",
        ),
        dmar_raw: acpi_table(b"DMAR"),
        ivrs_raw: acpi_table(b"IVRS"),
    }
}

//! The demo laptop must keep producing the findings shown in docs/demo.svg.
#![cfg(not(windows))]
use std::process::Command;

#[test]
fn laptop_fixture_findings() {
    let fx = concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/tests/fixtures/laptop");
    let out = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_dmaguard"))
        .args(["--json", "--root", fx])
        .output()
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(out.status.code(), Some(3));
    let v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&out.stdout).unwrap();
    let ids: Vec<&str> = v["findings"]
        .as_array()
        .unwrap()
        .iter()
        .map(|f| f["id"].as_str().unwrap())
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(
        ids,
        ["DMA-005", "DMA-002", "DMA-003", "DMA-016", "DMA-010", "DMA-013"]
    );
    assert_eq!(v["firmware"]["dmar"]["dma_ctrl_platform_opt_in"], false);
    assert_eq!(v["firmware"]["dmar"]["header"]["checksum_ok"], true);
}

`tools/gen_demo.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Record the tool's real terminal output into an animated docs/demo.svg.

Every step in tools/demo.json is executed for real (colours forced on), its
ANSI output is converted to styled text, and the session is played back as a
"filmstrip": each frame is a stack of <use> references to de-duplicated line
definitions, stepped through with a CSS keyframe animation. Nothing in the
demo is hand-written.

Usage: python3 tools/gen_demo.py            (run from the repository root)
"""
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from xml.sax.saxutils import escape

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CFG = json.loads((ROOT / "tools" / "demo.json").read_text())

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.home() / "github-profile" / "scripts"))
try:
    from brand import finish  # type: ignore  # embeds a JetBrains Mono subset
except Exception:  # pragma: no cover
    def finish(svg, faces=None):
        return svg

MONO = "'JBM','JetBrains Mono',ui-monospace,Consolas,Menlo,monospace"
PAL = {
    "text": "#C5CFDD", "dim": "#7C8AA0", "red": "#F87171", "green": "#34D399",
    "amber": "#FBBF24", "cyan": "#22D3EE", "blue": "#60A5FA", "white": "#F1F5FB",
    "crit": "#FFFFFF",
}
CW, FS, LH = 7.8, 13, 20
COLS = CFG.get("cols", 118)
ROWS = CFG.get("rows", 30)
VIEW_W, VIEW_H = int(COLS * CW) + 4, ROWS * LH + 6
W, H = VIEW_W + 36, VIEW_H + 76
SGR = re.compile(r"\x1b\[([0-9;]*)m")


def parse_ansi(line):
    """-> list of (text, colour, bold, critical-background)."""
    segs, color, bold, dim, bg = [], "text", False, False, False
    pos = 0
    for m in SGR.finditer(line):
        if m.start() > pos:
            segs.append((line[pos:m.start()], "dim" if dim and color == "text" else color, bold, bg))
        for code in (m.group(1) or "0").split(";"):
            c = int(code or 0)
            if c == 0:
                color, bold, dim, bg = "text", False, False, False
            elif c == 1:
                bold = True
            elif c == 2:
                dim = True
            elif c == 22:
                bold = dim = False
            elif c == 31 or c == 91:
                color = "red"
            elif c == 32 or c == 92:
                color = "green"
            elif c == 33 or c == 93:
                color = "amber"
            elif c == 36 or c == 96:
                color = "cyan"
            elif c == 34 or c == 94:
                color = "blue"
            elif c == 37 or c == 97:
                color = "white"
            elif c == 39:
                color = "text"
            elif c == 41:
                bg = True
            elif c == 49:
                bg = False
        pos = m.end()
    if pos < len(line):
        segs.append((line[pos:], "dim" if dim and color == "text" else color, bold, bg))
    return segs


def clip(segs, cols):
    out, n = [], 0
    for t, c, b, bg in segs:
        if n >= cols:
            break
        t = t[: cols - n]
        out.append((t, c, b, bg))
        n += len(t)
    return out


def prompt_segs(cmd):
    p = CFG["prompt"]
    return [(p["user"], "cyan", True, False), (":", "text", False, False),
            (p["path"], "blue", False, False), ("$ ", "text", False, False),
            (cmd, "white", False, False)]


def run(step):
    env = dict(os.environ, CLICOLOR_FORCE="1", COLUMNS=str(COLS))
    env.update(CFG.get("env", {}))
    r = subprocess.run(step["run"], shell=True, cwd=ROOT, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
    lines = (r.stdout + r.stderr).rstrip("\n").split("\n")
    if step.get("skip_blank_head"):
        while lines and not lines[0].strip():
            lines.pop(0)
    if "head" in step:
        lines = lines[: step["head"]]
    return [clip(parse_ansi(l.replace("\t", "    ")), COLS) for l in lines]


def build():
    screen, frames, durs = [], [], []

    def snap(d, extra=None):
        frames.append(screen[-ROWS:] if extra is None else (screen + [extra])[-ROWS:])
        durs.append(d)

    for step in CFG["steps"]:
        cmd = step["show"]
        for i in range(0, len(cmd) + 1, 2):
            snap(1, prompt_segs(cmd[:i] + "█"))
        snap(6, prompt_segs(cmd))
        screen.append(prompt_segs(cmd))
        out = run(step)
        chunk = step.get("chunk", 2)
        for i in range(0, len(out), chunk):
            screen.extend(out[i:i + chunk])
            snap(step.get("speed", 1))
        snap(step.get("hold", 30))
        screen.append([])
    snap(50, prompt_segs("█"))
    return frames, durs


def render():
    frames, durs = build()
    line_ids, defs = {}, []

    def lid(segs):
        key = tuple(segs)
        if key not in line_ids:
            n = len(line_ids)
            line_ids[key] = n
            parts, x = [f'<g id="l{n}">'], 0.0
            for t, c, b, bg in segs:
                if not t:
                    continue
                w = len(t) * CW
                if bg:
                    parts.append(f'<rect x="{x:.1f}" y="-14" width="{w:.1f}" height="18" fill="#B91C1C"/>')
                fill = PAL["crit"] if bg else PAL[c]
                wt = ' font-weight="700"' if b or bg else ""
                if t.strip():
                    parts.append(f'<text x="{x:.1f}" fill="{fill}"{wt} textLength="{w:.1f}" '
                                 f'lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">{escape(t)}</text>')
                x += w
            parts.append("</g>")
            defs.append("".join(parts))
        return line_ids[key]

    strip = []
    for i, fr in enumerate(frames):
        uses = "".join(f'<use href="#l{lid(seg)}" y="{16 + j * LH}"/>' for j, seg in enumerate(fr) if seg)
        strip.append(f'<g transform="translate(0,{i * VIEW_H})">{uses}</g>')

    total = sum(durs)
    cum, stops = 0, []
    for i, d in enumerate(durs):
        stops.append(f"{cum / total * 100:.3f}%{{transform:translateY(-{i * VIEW_H}px)}}")
        cum += d
    last = (len(durs) - 1) * VIEW_H
    stops.append(f"100%{{transform:translateY(-{last}px)}}")
    secs = max(12, round(total * 0.07))
    css = ("@keyframes play{" + "".join(stops) + "}"
           f".strip{{animation:play {secs}s steps(1,end) infinite}}"
           f"@media(prefers-reduced-motion){{.strip{{animation:none;transform:translateY(-{last}px)}}}}")

    title = escape(CFG["title"])
    svg = (
        f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{W}" height="{H}" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" '
        f'role="img" aria-label="{title}">'
        f'<style>{css}</style><defs>{"".join(defs)}</defs>'
        f'<rect x="0.5" y="0.5" width="{W - 1}" height="{H - 1}" rx="12" fill="#111826" stroke="#1E2A3D"/>'
        f'<path d="M0 40H{W}" stroke="#1E2A3D"/>'
        '<circle cx="24" cy="20" r="6" fill="#FF5F57"/><circle cx="44" cy="20" r="6" fill="#FEBC2E"/>'
        '<circle cx="64" cy="20" r="6" fill="#28C840"/>'
        f'<text x="{W / 2:.0f}" y="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="#8B98AD" font-family="{MONO}" font-size="13">{title}</text>'
        f'<svg x="18" y="54" width="{VIEW_W}" height="{VIEW_H}" viewBox="0 0 {VIEW_W} {VIEW_H}" overflow="hidden">'
        f'<g class="strip" font-family="{MONO}" font-size="{FS}" xml:space="preserve">{"".join(strip)}</g>'
        '</svg></svg>\n')
    return finish(svg, {("JBM", 400), ("JBM", 700)}), len(frames)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    out, n = render()
    p = ROOT / "docs" / "demo.svg"
    p.write_text(out, encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"wrote {p} ({len(out) // 1024} KB, {n} frames)")

```

`tools/make_fixture.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build tests/fixtures/laptop: /proc + /sys of a Thunderbolt laptop with a
weak DMA posture, used by docs/demo.svg.

  * ACPI DMAR: interrupt remapping yes, DMA_CTRL_PLATFORM_OPT_IN no,
    an RMRR on the onboard NIC (00:1f.6)
  * IOMMU on, but booted with iommu=pt (identity domains, lazy flush)
  * Thunderbolt domain security "none", iommu_dma_protection 0
  * an external dock's PCIe device attached

Usage: python3 tools/make_fixture.py
"""
import struct
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT = ROOT / "tests" / "fixtures" / "laptop"


def acpi(sig, extra, body):
    t = bytearray(sig + struct.pack("<IBB", 0, 1, 0) + b"CONTSO" + b"LAPTOP14" + struct.pack("<III", 1, 0x4C544E49, 1))
    t += extra + body
    t[4:8] = struct.pack("<I", len(t))
    t[9] = (-sum(t)) & 0xFF
    return bytes(t)


def dmar():
    hdr = bytes([38, 0b001]) + b"\0" * 10  # HAW 39 bits, INTR_REMAP only
    drhd = struct.pack("<HHBBHQ", 0, 16, 1, 0, 0, 0xFED91000)
    scope = bytes([1, 8, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x1F, 6])  # endpoint 00:1f.6
    rmrr = struct.pack("<HHHHQQ", 1, 24 + len(scope), 0, 0, 0x7B800000, 0x7BFFFFFF) + scope
    return acpi(b"DMAR", hdr, drhd + rmrr)


def w(rel, data):
    p = OUT / rel
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    p.write_bytes(data if isinstance(data, bytes) else data.encode())


def main():
    w("proc/sys/kernel/osrelease", "6.8.0-45-generic\n")
    w("proc/cmdline", "BOOT_IMAGE=/vmlinuz-6.8.0-45-generic root=/dev/nvme0n1p2 ro quiet splash iommu=pt\n")
    w("sys/firmware/acpi/tables/DMAR", dmar())
    w("sys/class/iommu/dmar0/.keep", "")
    for i, t in enumerate(["identity"] * 14 + ["DMA-FQ"] * 3):
        w(f"sys/kernel/iommu_groups/{i}/type", t + "\n")
    w("sys/bus/thunderbolt/devices/domain0/security", "none\n")
    w("sys/bus/thunderbolt/devices/domain0/iommu_dma_protection", "0\n")
    w("sys/bus/thunderbolt/devices/0-0/device_name", "Host router\n")
    w("sys/bus/thunderbolt/devices/0-1/vendor_name", "Contoso\n")
    w("sys/bus/thunderbolt/devices/0-1/device_name", "TB4 Dock\n")
    w("sys/bus/thunderbolt/devices/0-1/authorized", "1\n")
    # Real sysfs names this directory 0000:3c:00.0; ':' is invalid on NTFS,
    # so the snapshot uses a neutral name and the address lives in uevent.
    dev = "sys/bus/pci/devices/dock-nic"
    w(f"{dev}/uevent", "DRIVER=igc\nPCI_CLASS=20000\nPCI_SLOT_NAME=0000:3c:00.0\n")
    w(f"{dev}/removable", "removable\n")
    w(f"{dev}/vendor", "0x8086\n")
    w(f"{dev}/device", "0x15f2\n")
    w(f"{dev}/class", "0x020000\n")
    print("wrote", OUT)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```
